title: Analyte
applies_when: The procedure determines chemical composition. Omit for techniques that resolve no chemical species — imaging, tomography, sample preparation.
sub_module_test: Run 2026-08-14 under Rule 6.15. Footprint 13 consumers — every TAPP that determines a chemical composition. Prong 1 returned an IDENTICAL footprint against Module_Aggregation: the same 13 TAPPs, exactly. Prong 2 refused the merger. 'Which chemical species does this procedure determine' and 'which analyses contribute to the reported value' are not one subject, and a registrant hunting for the analyte list would not open a module about aggregation. The two conditions select the same TAPPs because determining a composition and aggregating analyses happen to co-occur across this library's techniques, not because they are one component — co-extension is not coherence. Core (16/16) cannot absorb it: Core is unconditional and Analyte is absent from Lab-XCT, SEM_FIBSEM and SEM_Imaging. No composition module is possible either — only three fields share this footprint and the other two are already Aggregation.
notes:
Single-field module, legitimate under Rule 6.10 as amended 2026-08-14: the threshold is ten placements (fields x consumers), and this is 13. Analyte previously belonged to no module, and was one of the seven near-universal fields the schema-generation work flagged as duplicated across the library.

Rule 7 is safe. In all 13 consumers Analyte is the sole `defines: analyte`; in the three TAPPs that omit it there is no definer AND no field keyed by `analyte`. The module's applicability condition and the Rule 7 invariant have the same footprint, so omitting the module can never strand a consumer with an undefined key.

Anchored on `Reported Variables and Units` — a Core field, present in all 16 and in the same group, so the anchor cannot go missing in a future consumer.
decisions: 2026-08-14 v1. Field text taken unchanged from the library, which was verified uniform across all 13 holders first; composition is therefore a no-op and no consumer needs a version bump.
Compose AFTER Core: the block anchors on Reported Variables and Units, owned by Core.

2026-08-14: source_comment declared. Rule 6.11 originally withheld the label from the general modules as noise; with 12 modules supplying most of the library, naming the source of every field is what makes a composed TAPP readable. Documentation only — no structural meaning, not schema content.

2026-08-25: Column J `Purpose` declared as an OVERLAY column, not an owned one. The module supplies a default Purpose that a consumer inherits on composition and owns thereafter — the same relationship Column F already has. Added after Step 1 stripped Purpose sentences from Module_ArAr's descriptions with nowhere to put them, because ArAr is composed into no TAPP: a module with no consumer had no destination for its own Purpose text, so the text was lost. Modules now hold it themselves.
